description:

> Which issue, if any, is this issue related to?

Part of https://github.com/stylelint/stylelint/issues/6869

> Is there anything in the PR that needs further explanation?

No, it's self-explanatory.

human_review_comments.author: romainmenke
human_review_comments.body:
```suggestion
const HAS_TIME = /\d(?:m?)s/i;
```

Slightly simpler regex that should also be slightly faster?

human_review_comments.author: jeddy3
human_review_comments.body:
We'll need to allow for `ms`, too.

A slightly more complicated one that makes this explicit could be:

```
\d+(?:\.\d+)?(?:ms|s)
```

Allows: `200ms`, `0.2s` etc.

human_review_comments.author: romainmenke
human_review_comments.body:
Right! I did forget about `ms`.

I think this should be fine: `\d(?:m?)s`
We don't need to test for more than one digit or decimals.

Any last digit followed by either `ms` or `s` is likely to be a dimension with a time unit.

title: Fix `no-duplicate-selectors` false negatives for matching escaped selectors
description:
## Summary

Fixes #3972

The `no-duplicate-selectors` rule now correctly detects duplicate class selectors that use different CSS escape sequence formats. For example, `.u-m\00002b` and `.u-m\+` are now recognized as duplicates since both represent `.u-m+`.

## Changes

- Added `normalizeNodeEscaping()` helper in `normalizeSelector.mjs` that uses postcss-selector-parser's getter/setter behavior to normalize CSS escaping
- Added test cases for escaped selector duplicates

## How it works

The fix leverages postcss-selector-parser's built-in value getter/setter behavior for ClassName nodes. The getter returns the unescaped value, while the setter re-escapes it in a normalized form. By doing `node.value = node.value`, we trigger this normalization, ensuring equivalent selectors compare as equal regardless of their original escape format.

Reference: https://github.com/postcss/postcss-selector-parser/blob/1b1e9c3bc10ccc3bc5f07a987caa7f2684c0b52f/src/selectors/className.js#L13-L28

ryo-manba
human_review_comments.body:
[Q] Is this PR scoped to ClassName only?
It might be difficult to support ID and attribute selectors due to limitations in `postcss-selector-parser` 🤔

title: Fix `declaration-property-value-no-unknown` performance
description:
<!-- Each pull request must be associated with an open issue unless it's a documentation fix. If a corresponding issue does not exist, please create one so we can discuss the change first. -->

<!-- Please answer the following. We close pull requests that don't. -->

> Which issue, if any, is this issue related to?

Similar to https://github.com/stylelint/stylelint/pull/9061

> Is there anything in the PR that needs further explanation?

This PR changes the rule to only call `fork` if the `*syntax` secondary options are used, or if the file being linted contains `@property` at-rules extending the syntax, otherwise the rule uses the cached lexer from `context`.

I'll open an issue to remove the (now redundant since we added `languageOption`) secondary options, so only the more performant `languageOption` is available. It seems forking on new definitions in a file is unavoidable, though.

Benchmarked using our standard config:

```
export default {
	extends: ['stylelint-config-standard'],
};
```

Nearly halves the time when running our config on 1000 CSS files:


human_review_comments.body: [question] `atrules: languageOptions?.syntax?.atRules` seems to be removed, but no problem?

human_review_comments.author: romainmenke
human_review_comments.body:
From a syntax definition perspective this should be fine.
We don't use the at-rule syntaxes directly when validating declarations.

In theory there could be a dependency on at-rule definitions, but no such dependency exists today as far as I know.

It would be slightly safer to always include the entire syntax definition in each rule that uses the lexer.
